verdict: The four slices were INCOMPLETE and NOT ASSEMBLABLE, but the parts that exist are high quality. Three structural defects, all measured, all now fixed: (1) 162 of en.json's 590 keys were claimed by NO slice — including four of the headline defects the phase was chartered to fix (GMONLY=仅限通用汽车, Overwatch=守望先锋, HOWMANYDICE=有多少基地死亡？, Utility=公用事业) plus five more roll→滚动 keys; (2) 57 keys were claimed by TWO OR THREE slices, 29 of them with different Chinese, and the project's own apply_lang.py has no cross-batch conflict detection (apply_lang.py:206 is a bare set_path) so assembly was 59 silent overwrites with zero log output — measured: 505 entries in, 487 "applied", 446 actually distinct; (3) lang-ui's 18 code-only keys were rejected wholesale by apply_lang.py:170 (`if key not in en`). Constraint compliance is otherwise clean and I could not break it: the 8 crit-parse keys are byte-exact English, registered in lang_keep_english.json with per-key actor.mjs line numbers, and the never_write entry is respected; all 12 T-EXACT skill names are byte-equal to glossary_alien.json (incl. Comtech=通信科技 per R3), distinct, unpadded, pure CJK, each carrying requires_pack_rename:true; zero frozen-literal collisions including the six .toUpperCase() talent names tested the way the code does it; placeholders and HTML tag multisets 1:1 across all 584 keys. After my fixes: 584 of 590 en.json keys covered by exactly one slice each, 6 deliberately unwritten with reasons, apply_lang.py --dry reports 584 applied / 0 rejected / 0 overwrites, and my 9-gate battery reports 0 failures.

missed_items.why_matters: Every future parallel wave hits this. The slice-boundary discipline in PARALLEL-RUNBOOK.md is the only thing preventing it, and it demonstrably did not hold for four agents on one 590-key file. apply_lang.py should refuse — or at minimum warn — when a key appears in more than one batch with a different value.
